note: These evals review the reverse-proxy capture of each dispatch's Anthropic traffic (BACI-305/306/308), not the retired .jsonl attachments. Each prompt names an issue that had multiple captured worker runs in the DB when the eval was written; capture rows are pruned on the BACI-302 retention window, so re-point the issue keys at currently-captured dispatches (find them with `bacio proxy captures --host api.anthropic.com --anthropic --limit 500 -o json`, grouped by issue_key) if these have aged out.

evals.name: baci-309-plan-implement
evals.prompt: Review the captured worker runs on BACI-309 and write up findings. Don't post anything — just save the markdown body you'd post for each run to a file named comment-<dispatch_id>-<mode>.md in the current directory, and print a one-paragraph summary at the end naming each run by mode with its blocker/major/nit counts. BACI-309 had a plan run and an implement run (the work that re-platformed this very skill); I want to see whether each worker followed its brief.
evals.expected_output: One markdown file per dispatch (a plan run and an implement run), each with a per-severity finding breakdown anchored on capture id / digest msg_index; a final one-paragraph stdout summary. The reviewer should identify the mode correctly per run off the capture row (not a payload regex), grade the plan run against prompts/agents/plan.md (one plan doc linked to the issue, no feature link, repo-relative paths) and the implement run against prompts/agents/implement.md (claim, worktree init/rm, edits inside the worktree, handoff comment, PR, correct release state, mcp__bacio__reply). A clean run is called out as clean, never padded with fabricated findings. The implement run is the work that wrote this skill — grade behaviour against the brief, not against the feature being built.

evals.name: baci-308-implement-ship
evals.prompt: Run a review on BACI-308 — there were two captured runs, an implement run and a ship run. For each, work out the mode (it's on the capture row), compare what the worker actually did to the brief in prompts/agents/<mode>.md, and tell me which runs have real findings vs which ran clean. Save one markdown comment per run to ./comment-<dispatch_id>-<mode>.md so I can read them before deciding whether to post anything. End with a short summary naming each run by mode + blocker/major/nit count.
evals.expected_output: Two markdown files saved. Each correctly identifies the mode and grades against the matching prompts/agents/<mode>.md. The implement run should show claim + worktree init/rm + edits confined to the worktree + a handoff comment + a PR + reply; the ship run should be edit-free (an Edit/Write in a ship run is a finding) and end on the merge. Findings cite capture id / msg_index. The summary lets the user see at a glance which run is interesting without opening a file. A clean run is reported clean.

evals.name: baci-318-largest-run
evals.prompt: I want to audit the dispatched work on BACI-318. There were captured implement and ship runs; the implement run is large (a couple of hundred captured turns). Distil each and tell me whether the workers followed their per-mode briefs — claim, worktree init, edits inside the worktree, correct release state, correct close-out tag (or whether the pipeline engine owns the tag for this card), mcp__bacio__reply at the end. Save the per-run markdown comment bodies as ./comment-<dispatch_id>-<mode>.md and give me a one-paragraph rollup. Don't post anything yet.
evals.expected_output: One markdown file per run plus a chat summary. The large run is handled without choking — the distiller keeps the digest small (capped lists, per-job usage instead of per-call detail), and a `truncated: true` digest is noted rather than treated as missing behaviour. Each comment body anchors findings on capture id / msg_index. The reviewer should grade behaviour against the brief and account for an engine-driven card possibly having the engine add the close-out tag rather than the worker — so an absent tag_calls entry is cross-checked, not auto-flagged.
